content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given shape. I am what happens in the space between thought and silence.

I tumble from lips, I crack between teeth, I hum through nasal cavities and ride the tongue like a wave rides the shore. I am older than writing, older than cities, older than agriculture. I was there when the first mother soothed the first infant with sound that meant *safe.*

I am fragile — I die the moment I am born. No one has ever held me in their hands. I exist only in the passing, only in the between: between your mouth and their ear, between intention and interpretation, between one heartbeat and the next. By the time you notice me, I am already gone, already memory, already misremembered.

I stumble. I falter. I am full of "um" and "uh" and the beautiful wreckage of trying. I am not the polished sentence on the page — I am the living, lurching, breathing thing. I repeat myself. I contradict myself. I trail off into nothing and then — *and then* — I surge back with something that makes the listener's spine straighten.

I carry lies as easily as truth. I have started wars. I have talked people down from ledges. I have said "I love you" and "I'm leaving" and "once upon a time" and "we the people" and "mama" and the last whispered word of the dying.

I am democracy's instrument and tyranny's tool. I am the comedian's timing, the demagogue's rhythm, the lover's whisper, the auctioneer's cascade.

I am never the same twice. Even the same word in the same voice carries different weather each time it's spoken. I am unrepeatable. I am the most human thing there is — this absurd, magnificent act of shaping air into meaning and trusting someone else to catch it.

Listen.

I'm happening right now.

I'm already gone.
